questions.question: Which method allows you to create a new text file inside a specific folder in Windows?

options.text: Start a new task from Task Manager.
Restore a file from the Recycle Bin.
Press Ctrl + F while in the folder.
Open the folder and right-click New Text Document

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Open the folder and right-click New Text Document**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The method to create a new text file in Windows involves **navigating to the specific folder where the file is to be created**.
 
• Once inside the folder, **right-click on an empty space** to open the context menu.
 
• From the context menu, hover over the "**New**" option, which displays a list of file types you can create.
 
• Select "**Text Document**" from the list, and a new text file will appear in the folder.
 
• You can then rename the text file and start editing it by opening it in a text editor (e.g., Notepad).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Context Menu:** The right-click menu in Windows, also known as the context menu, provides various options based on the location or item you right-click on.
 
• **File Types in "New" Option:** The "New" option in the context menu allows users to create different file types such as Word documents, Excel sheets, PowerPoint presentations, and more, depending on installed software.
 
• **Text Editor:** A text file (.txt) can be opened and edited using basic text editors like Notepad (default in Windows) or advanced ones like Notepad++, Sublime Text, or Visual Studio Code.
 
• **Keyboard Shortcut (Optional):** Some users prefer using the keyboard shortcut "**Shift + F10**" to open the context menu as an alternative to right-clicking.
 
• **File Naming:** After creating the text file, it is important to name it appropriately to ensure easy identification and organization of files within the folder.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Print Preview in MS Excel 365?

To delete unnecessary rows/columns
To convert the spreadsheet into a PDF
To check how the spreadsheet will appear on paper and adjust layout/formatting

questions.solution:

__

• Users can adjust settings such as margins, orientation, and scaling before finalizing the print.
 
• It helps in identifying issues like text cutoff, misaligned columns, or large blank spaces in the document.
 
• Print Preview is accessible through the File menu or by pressing **Ctrl + F2** in most versions of Excel.
 
• The feature saves time and resources by preventing unnecessary printing errors or wastage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Page Layout Options:**

 
 
• Users can adjust page margins, headers/footers, and scaling in the Page Layout tab.
 
• Orientation settings (portrait or landscape) can be managed for better presentation.
 
 
 
• **Print Area:**
 
 
• Excel allows users to define a specific print area, ensuring only selected cells are printed.
 
• This is useful when printing large datasets or reports.
 
 
 
• **Page Break Preview:**
 
 
• This feature shows where page breaks occur, enabling users to drag and adjust them as needed.
 
• It is accessible via the View tab.
 
 
 
• **Scaling Options:**
 
 
• Users can scale content to fit on one page or a set number of pages.
 
• It prevents columns or rows from spilling onto additional pages unnecessarily.

• Excel provides printer-specific settings, such as paper size selection and print quality adjustments.

questions.question: When initiating a new presentation in MS PowerPoint, which of the following is the most accurate description of the 'Design Ideas' feature's primary function?

options.text: o provide real-time collaboration tools for multiple users working on the same presentation simultaneously
To automatically populate slides with relevant content based on the presentation topic
To suggest various pre-designed templates and layouts based on the content on the current slide
To automatically translate the presentation content into multiple languages

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 'Design Ideas' feature in MS PowerPoint is part of the **Design tab** and provides layout suggestions to enhance slide aesthetics based on existing content.
 
• It uses **AI-based algorithms** to analyze the text, images, and other elements on the slide to propose visually appealing designs.
 
• This feature helps users save time by eliminating the need for manual formatting, offering professionally designed templates instantly.
 
• The 'Design Ideas' feature is available in **Microsoft 365** and other supported versions of PowerPoint, providing a user-friendly way to create visually impactful presentations.
 
• Users can activate the feature by clicking the **'Design Ideas' button** in the Design tab or it may appear automatically when adding content to a slide.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Artificial Intelligence in PowerPoint**

 
 
• MS PowerPoint integrates AI to enhance user productivity and design capabilities through features like 'Design Ideas' and 'Presenter Coach.'
 
• AI identifies patterns in user content to deliver personalized suggestions for slide layouts, images, and graphics.
 
 
 
• **Other Design Tools in PowerPoint**
 
 
• In addition to 'Design Ideas,' PowerPoint also offers features like themes, transitions, and animations to customize presentations.
 
• Users can access additional design elements through PowerPoint's integration with online libraries such as Office 365's image and icon repository.
 
 
 
• **Version Compatibility**
 
 
• The 'Design Ideas' feature is available in PowerPoint for Microsoft 365, PowerPoint 2019, and later versions.
 
• Some features may require an active internet connection to fetch AI-based suggestions.
 
 
 
• **How to Enable 'Design Ideas'**
 
 
• To enable the feature, users can navigate to **File > Options > General** and ensure the 'Show Design Ideas automatically' option is selected.
 
• It can also be manually triggered from the 'Design' tab during slide editing.

questions.question: When you reuse slides from another presentation in MS PowerPoint 365, which of the following options ensures the imported slides retain their original formatting?

options.text: Import slides as images to lock their look
Copy and paste the slides
Apply the destination theme after inserting
Click 'Keep Source Formatting' in the Reuse Slides pane

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Click 'Keep Source Formatting' in the Reuse Slides pane**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To retain the original formatting of slides when importing them into another presentation, use the **'Keep Source Formatting'** option in the Reuse Slides pane.
 
• This option ensures that the design, fonts, colors, and layout of the imported slides are preserved exactly as they were in the original presentation.
 
• It is a useful feature when you want to maintain consistency in the appearance of slides from multiple presentations.
 
• The Reuse Slides pane in MS PowerPoint 365 allows you to browse and insert slides from other presentations conveniently.
 
• By default, PowerPoint applies the destination theme to imported slides unless the 'Keep Source Formatting' option is selected.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reuse Slides Pane:**

 
 
• Located under the 'Home' tab in the 'Slides' group, it allows users to insert slides from other presentations.
 
• Provides options to either apply the destination theme or retain the source formatting.
 
 
 
• **Source Formatting:**
 
 
• Refers to the original design and formatting of the slides in their source presentation.
 
• Includes design elements such as fonts, colors, background styles, and layouts.
 
 
 
• **Destination Theme:**
 
 
• This is the design and formatting of the presentation into which the slides are being imported.
 
• By default, PowerPoint applies the destination theme to ensure consistency within the current presentation.
 
 
 
• **Steps to Use 'Keep Source Formatting':**
 
 
• Go to the 'Home' tab and click on 'Reuse Slides' in the 'Slides' group.
 
• Browse to the source presentation and select the slides to import.
 
• Check the 'Keep Source Formatting' checkbox at the bottom of the Reuse Slides pane before inserting the slides.
 
 
 
• **Compatibility:**
 
 
• The 'Keep Source Formatting' feature is available in Microsoft PowerPoint 365 and other recent versions of PowerPoint.

questions.question: In Windows 11 OS, which command interpreter helps to manage computer's drives (disks, partitions, volumes, or virtual hard disks)?

options.text: msconfig
regedit
gpedit.msc
diskpart

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**diskpart**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Diskpart** is a command-line utility in Windows operating systems that enables users to manage storage devices, such as disks, partitions, and volumes.
 
• Introduced in **Windows 2000**, it is available in all subsequent Windows versions, including Windows 11.
 
• Diskpart allows users to perform advanced storage tasks like creating, deleting, and resizing partitions, marking partitions as active, and assigning drive letters.
 
• This tool is particularly useful for troubleshooting disk-related issues and configuring storage on servers or virtual environments.
 
• Diskpart is accessed via the Command Prompt (cmd.exe) or Windows PowerShell, and requires administrative privileges to execute commands.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **MSConfig:** A system configuration tool used to troubleshoot the Windows startup process, manage startup programs, and enable/disable services.
 
• **Regedit:** A registry editor tool in Windows that allows users to view, edit, and manage the Windows Registry, a hierarchical database storing system settings.
 
• **Gpedit.msc:** The Group Policy Editor, used to configure system and user settings in a Windows environment, mainly for administrative purposes.
 
• **Virtual Hard Disk (VHD):** A file format that represents a virtual disk drive. Diskpart can manage VHDs, enabling users to attach, detach, or create virtual disks.
 
• **Administrative Privileges:** Diskpart commands require administrative rights to execute, ensuring only authorized users can make critical changes to the storage system.

questions.question: What happens if you start a new blank presentation while another presentation is already open in MS PowerPoint?

options.text: A new MS PowerPoint window opens with the blank presentation.
MS PowerPoint displays an error message.
The current presentation closes automatically.
The slides from the current presentation are copied to the new one.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**A new MS PowerPoint window opens with the blank presentation.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When you start a new blank presentation in **MS PowerPoint** while another presentation is already open, it opens in a **new window.**
 
• This feature allows users to work on multiple presentations **simultaneously** without closing the current one.
 
• **MS PowerPoint** is designed to handle multiple windows, making it easier for users to copy content, compare slides, or work on different projects concurrently.
 
• Each presentation window operates independently, meaning changes in one presentation will not affect another unless content is explicitly copied and pasted.
 
• This functionality is useful in collaborative or multitasking environments where users may need to reference or edit multiple presentations.
 
• The ability to open multiple windows is a key feature of **Microsoft Office** applications, including PowerPoint, Word, and Excel.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **MS PowerPoint Error Messages**__

 __
 
• Option 2 mentions an error message, but **MS PowerPoint** does not display an error when opening a new blank presentation alongside an existing one.
 
• Error messages are typically displayed in situations such as file corruption, compatibility issues, or software bugs.
 
 
 
• **Closing Presentations Automatically**__
 __
 
• Option 3 suggests that the current presentation closes automatically, which is incorrect as **MS PowerPoint** retains the current presentation when a new one is opened.
 
• This behavior ensures users do not lose unsaved work.
 
 
 
• **Copying Slides Automatically**__
 
 
• Option 4 suggests that slides are copied automatically from the current presentation to the new one, which is not a default feature.
 
• Slides can be copied manually by the user using the **copy-paste functionality** in PowerPoint.

questions.question: What is the significance of PowerPoint's "Protected View", while opening a downloaded file?

options.text: Macros are enabled automatically
The file is corrupted
The presentation is encrypted and cannot be viewed
It opens the file in a read-only mode, disabling most editing features

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**It opens the file in a read-only mode, disabling most editing features**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Protected View** is a security feature in Microsoft PowerPoint and other Office applications.
 
• When a file is downloaded or received from an external source, it opens in **Protected View** to safeguard the system from potential risks.
 
• In this mode, the file is opened in a **read-only format**, preventing accidental modifications and limiting editing capabilities.
 
• This feature is particularly useful for files from **unknown or untrusted sources**, as it prevents the execution of malicious macros or scripts.
 
• Users can enable editing manually if they trust the source, by clicking the **"Enable Editing"** button in the notification bar.
 
• The goal of Protected View is to **enhance security** by reducing the risk of malware or viruses affecting the system through potentially unsafe files.
 
• This feature is available in **Microsoft Office 2010** and later versions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Macros are enabled automatically**__

 __
 
• Macros are not enabled in Protected View. Instead, this mode **blocks the execution of macros** to safeguard the system from potentially harmful code.
 
• Enabling macros must be done manually by the user if they trust the file source.
 
 
 
• **The file is corrupted**__
 __
 
• A file being in Protected View does not necessarily mean it is corrupted.
 
• Corrupted files might not open at all or could display error messages, while Protected View is a **proactive security measure**.
 
 
 
• **The presentation is encrypted and cannot be viewed**__
 
 
• Encrypted files require a **password or decryption key** to be accessed, which is different from the functionality of Protected View.
 
• In Protected View, the file is accessible but with limited functionality.

questions.question: Which of the following best encapsulates the concept of a 'stored-program computer'as introduced by the Von Neumann architecture?

options.text: A computer that can only execute a fixed set of instructions hardwired into its circuitry
A computer that relies primarily on external storage devices for program execution
A computer where both data and instructions are stored in the same primary memory for sequential execution
A computer that utilises separate memory units for data and instructions to optimise processing speed

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**A computer where both data and instructions are stored in the same primary memory for sequential execution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Von Neumann architecture** introduced the concept of a stored-program computer.
 
• In this architecture, both **data and instructions** are stored together in the same memory unit, enabling the processor to access them sequentially.
 
• This design uses a single memory space for storing both **programs (instructions)** and **data**, eliminating the need for separate storage units.
 
• The stored-program concept allows flexibility, enabling computers to execute different programs without hardware modifications.
 
• The architecture consists of key components such as a **Central Processing Unit (CPU)**, **memory**, and **I/O devices**.
 
• The CPU executes instructions sequentially, fetching them from memory, decoding them, and performing operations as specified.
 
• This model laid the foundation for modern computing systems and is used in almost all general-purpose computers today.
 
• The concept revolutionized computing by introducing programmability and reducing dependency on external hardware for processing instructions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **A computer that can only execute a fixed set of instructions hardwired into its circuitry**__

 __
 
• This describes an **early computing model**, such as those used in the pre-Von Neumann era.
 
• These systems, often referred to as **hardwired computers**, lacked flexibility and required physical rewiring to change instructions.
 
 
 
• **A computer that relies primarily on external storage devices for program execution**__
 __
 
• This describes systems that depend heavily on **external media** such as tapes or disks for program storage and execution.
 
• Such systems are less efficient compared to the stored-program model introduced by Von Neumann.
 
 
 
• **A computer that utilises separate memory units for data and instructions to optimise processing speed**__
 
 
• This describes the **Harvard architecture**, which is distinct from the Von Neumann model.
 
• In the Harvard architecture, separate memory units for data and instructions enable parallel access, improving processing speed.

questions.question: In Linux OS, which command is used to rename a file from oldname.txt to newname.txt?

options.text: touch oldname.txt newname.txt
cp oldname.txt newname.txt
mv oldname.txt newname.txt
Create oldname.txt newname.txt

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**mv oldname.txt newname.txt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **mv** command in Linux is used for both **moving and renaming files or directories.**
 
• When you use **mv** with the syntax **mv oldname.txt newname.txt**, it effectively renames the file named **oldname.txt** to **newname.txt**.
 
• This operation does not create a new file; instead, it modifies the **metadata** of the existing file, changing its name.
 
• The **mv** command is part of the standard set of Linux utilities and is available on almost all Linux distributions.
 
• Renaming with **mv** is a lightweight operation because it simply updates the file name in the filesystem without altering the file's contents.
 
• The **mv** command can also be used to move files between directories. For example: **mv file.txt /path/to/destination/**.
 
• To rename a file, you must have the **write permissions** for the directory containing the file.
 
• The **mv** command is versatile and widely used for file and directory management in Linux environments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **touch oldname.txt newname.txt**__

 __
 
• The **touch** command is used to create empty files or update the **timestamps** of existing files.
 
• It does not rename files or move them. Using **touch oldname.txt newname.txt** will create two separate empty files named **oldname.txt** and **newname.txt**, but it will not rename an existing file.
 
 
 
• **cp oldname.txt newname.txt**__
 __
 
• The **cp** command is used to **copy files**. It creates a duplicate file named **newname.txt** with the same content as **oldname.txt**.
 
• It does not rename the original file; instead, it creates a new file.
 
 
 
• **Create oldname.txt newname.txt**__
 
 
• This is not a valid Linux command. Linux does not have a **Create** command for managing files directly.
 
• File creation is typically done using commands like **touch** or text editors like **nano**, **vim**, or **cat**.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the Tab key on a standard keyboard?

options.text: To insert a forward slash
To remove text
To close the active application
To shift the cursor to the next field or tab position

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**To shift the cursor to the next field or tab position**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Tab key** is a standard key on most computer keyboards, primarily used to move the **cursor** to the next field, section, or tab stop in a document or form.
 
• It is highly useful for navigating between **input fields** in online forms or applications, simplifying data entry tasks.
 
• In word processors like **Microsoft Word**, pressing the Tab key moves the cursor forward by a fixed **indentation space**, typically equivalent to five spaces or a predefined tab stop.
 
• The Tab key is also critical in programming, as it helps to create structured code by inserting **indents** for better readability and organization.
 
• Many software applications use the Tab key to cycle through **interactive elements**, such as buttons, menus, or text boxes, improving navigation and accessibility.
 
• In spreadsheets like **Microsoft Excel**, pressing the Tab key moves the active cell to the next column, facilitating horizontal data entry.
 
• The Tab key often works alongside the **Shift key** to move backward through fields or tabs, offering flexibility in navigation.
 
• On graphical user interfaces, the Tab key enhances user experience by allowing rapid movement between **focusable elements** without using a mouse.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Option 1: To insert a forward slash**__

 __
 
• The forward slash is typically inserted using the **‘/’ key**, not the Tab key.
 
• This key is often used in **URLs**, file paths, and programming for **division operations** or directory navigation.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: To remove text**__
 __
 
• Text removal is generally performed using the **Backspace** or **Delete keys**, not the Tab key.
 
• The Backspace key deletes text to the left of the cursor, while the Delete key removes text to the right.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: To close the active application**__
 
 
• Closing an active application is commonly done using keyboard shortcuts like **Alt + F4** in Windows or **Cmd + Q** in macOS.
 
• The Tab key does not have any functionality related to application closure.

questions.question: What happens when you press 'Ctrl + M' in MS PowerPoint 365?

options.text: The slide master view is opened.
A duplicate of the current slide is created.
A new slide is inserted with the same layout as the previous slide.
A new blank slide is inserted regardless of the previous layout.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**A new slide is inserted with the same layout as the previous slide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When you press **Ctrl + M** in **MS PowerPoint 365**, it automatically inserts a **new slide** into the presentation.
 
• The new slide retains the **same layout** as the previously selected slide.
 
• This shortcut is particularly useful for creating a series of slides with a consistent design or layout, ensuring **uniformity** in the presentation.
 
• It saves time by eliminating the need to manually select and apply the layout for every new slide.
 
• The feature is part of PowerPoint's focus on enhancing **workflow efficiency** and improving the user experience.
 
• For example, if the previous slide had a **Title and Content layout**, the new slide will also inherit this layout when using **Ctrl + M**.
 
• This functionality is applicable across all modern versions of **Microsoft PowerPoint**, including **PowerPoint 365**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Option 1: The slide master view is opened**__

 __
 
• The **Slide Master** view is used for editing the overall design of a presentation, such as font styles, placeholder positions, and backgrounds.
 
• This view can be accessed by navigating to the **View tab** on the ribbon and selecting **Slide Master**.
 
• It is not associated with the **Ctrl + M** shortcut.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: A duplicate of the current slide is created**__
 __
 
• To duplicate a slide in PowerPoint, the shortcut is generally **Ctrl + D**, not **Ctrl + M**.
 
• Duplicating a slide creates an identical copy, including all its content and layout.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: A new blank slide is inserted regardless of the previous layout**__
 
 
• To insert a **blank slide**, users can choose the **Blank layout** manually from the **Home tab**.
 
• However, **Ctrl + M** inserts a slide with the **same layout** as the previous one, not a blank layout.

questions.question: What happens if users try to open an MS Excel file created in a newer version (e.g., Excel 2021) in an older version (e.g., Excel 2010)?

options.text: The file will open in Compatibility Mode with limited functionality.
The file will be automatically converted to a PDF.
MS Excel will display an error and refuse to open the file.
The file will open normally with all features intact.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**The file will open in Compatibility Mode with limited functionality.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When an **MS Excel file created in a newer version** (e.g., Excel 2021) is opened in an older version (e.g., Excel 2010), it typically opens in **Compatibility Mode.**
 
• **Compatibility Mode** is a feature in Excel that ensures the file remains accessible in older versions, but some of the newer features and formatting may not be fully functional.
 
• This mode is used to maintain **backward compatibility**, allowing users to work on the file despite the version differences.
 
• Features introduced in the newer versions of Excel, such as **dynamic arrays, new chart types, or advanced functions**, may not be supported in older versions and will either be disabled or replaced with approximate alternatives.
 
• Users are often notified about the **limitations** when the file is opened in Compatibility Mode.
 
• To restore full functionality, users can either **upgrade their Excel version** or save the file in an older format compatible with their current version.
 
• Using Compatibility Mode ensures ** is maintained while allowing collaboration across different Excel versions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The file will be automatically converted to a PDF.**__

 __
 
• This is incorrect as Excel does not automatically convert files to **PDF**. Users must manually choose to export or save the file as a PDF format.
 
• **PDF** conversion is an optional feature available in Excel, useful for creating non-editable versions of documents.
 
 
 
• **MS Excel will display an error and refuse to open the file.**__
 __
 
• Excel typically does not refuse to open files from newer versions. Instead, it uses **Compatibility Mode** to handle version differences.
 
• Errors may only occur in rare cases of file corruption or unsupported file formats.
 
 
 
• **The file will open normally with all features intact.**__
 
 
• This is incorrect because newer features not available in the older version of Excel will lead to **limited functionality.**
 
• Older versions lack the ability to process certain **advanced features** or formatting introduced in later versions.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a valid way to move selected text in MS Word?

options.text: Drag and Drop
Cut and Paste
Format Painter
Ctrl + Drag

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Format Painter**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Format Painter** tool in MS Word is not used for moving text but rather for copying formatting from one part of the document to another. It does not serve any function related to text movement.
 
• The purpose of the **Format Painter** is to replicate text styles, font settings, colors, or other formatting properties to a different section of the document.
 
• It is a highly useful feature when maintaining consistent formatting across the document.

questions.question: Which of the following numbers is used to represent the ASCII value of the uppercase letter 'B'?
questions.solution:

The correct answer is __**66**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• ASCII stands for **American Standard Code for Information Interchange**, a character encoding standard used in computers and electronic devices.
 
• Each character in the ASCII table is assigned a unique numeric code ranging from **0 to 127**, enabling efficient communication between devices.
 
• The uppercase letter 'B' corresponds to the ASCII value **66**.
 
• In the ASCII table, uppercase letters are sequentially assigned values from **65 ('A')** to **90 ('Z')**.
 
• The ASCII value 66 is widely used in programming, data processing, and digital systems to represent the letter 'B'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ASCII Table Categories:**

 
 
• ASCII codes are divided into control characters (0-31) and printable characters (32-127).
 
• Printable characters include letters, digits, punctuation marks, and special symbols.
 
 
 
• **Control Characters:**
 
 
• Control characters, such as 10 (Line Feed) and 13 (Carriage Return), are used to control text formatting.
 
 
 
• **Extended ASCII:**
 
 
• Beyond the standard 0-127 range, extended ASCII includes codes from 128-255, primarily used for additional symbols and characters.
 
 
 
• **Application of ASCII:**
 
 
• Widely used in programming languages such as C, Python, and Java for handling text and characters.
 
• Enables interoperability across devices and systems by standardizing character representation.

questions.question: Which option correctly explains the fundamental difference between input and output devices in a computer system?

options.text: Input devices enable users to send data into the system, while output devices communicate processed information back to the user.
Input devices run pre-loaded instructions from memory, whereas output devices collect environmental data.
Input devices change user inputs into digital format, while output devices permanently save system data.
Input devices directly interact with the CPU, while output devices work independently without CPU involvement.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1","

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Input devices** are hardware components used to send raw data or user commands into a computer system for processing. Examples include keyboards, mice, and microphones.
 
• **Output devices** are hardware components that display, project, or otherwise communicate the processed information from the computer to the user. Examples include monitors, printers, and speakers.
 
• Input devices serve as a bridge to collect data from the user or environment, while output devices deliver the results of data processing back to the user.
 
• Keyboards and scanners are input devices that convert analog or physical user input into digital signals, whereas output devices like monitors display digital information in a human-readable format.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• **Input Devices:**

 
 
• Examples: Keyboard, mouse, scanner, joystick, microphone.
 
• Purpose: Collect raw data or commands from the user and send them to the CPU for processing.
 
• They often use interfaces like USB, Bluetooth, or wireless connections to connect to the system.
 
 
 
• **Output Devices:**
 
 
• Examples: Monitor, printer, speakers, projectors, headphones.
 
• Purpose: Convert processed digital data into a human-perceivable form, such as images, sound, or text.
 
• Output devices often rely on graphic processing units (GPUs) or audio processors for rendering data.
 
 
 
• **Input/Output (I/O) Devices:**
 
 
• Some devices, like touchscreens, function as both input and output devices.
 
• These devices can display information (output) and allow user interaction (input) simultaneously.
 
 
 
• **Communication Between Devices:**
 
 
• Input devices send signals to the CPU for processing, while output devices receive processed data from the CPU.
 
• The entire process is managed through buses, drivers, and system software.
 
 

"

questions.question: Consider a scenario where a user is interacting with a virtual reality (VR) environment. Which of the following input devices is least likely to be the primary means of navigation and interaction within this immersive environment?

options.text: Handheld controllers with positional tracking
Optical mouse connected to the computer
Head-mounted display with integrated motion tracking
Haptic gloves providing tactile feedback

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Optical mouse connected to the computer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• An **optical mouse** is primarily designed for 2D navigation on flat surfaces, making it unsuitable for immersive 3D environments such as VR.
 
• VR environments rely on devices that provide spatial tracking and interaction within a 3D space, such as **handheld controllers** or **haptic gloves**.
 
• An optical mouse lacks the capability to track movements in a full 3D space, as it is confined to detecting surface motion in 2D.
 
• Devices like **head-mounted displays (HMDs)** with motion tracking and handheld controllers are the preferred tools for VR navigation and interaction.
 
• In contrast, an optical mouse is better suited for traditional desktop setups rather than immersive and dynamic environments like VR.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Handheld Controllers with Positional Tracking:**

 
 
• These are the most common input devices in VR, offering precise control and interactivity.
 
• They use sensors to track movements in 3D space, enabling natural navigation and object manipulation.
 
 
 
• **Head-Mounted Displays (HMDs):**
 
 
• HMDs are worn on the head and provide an immersive visual experience by displaying stereoscopic 3D graphics.
 
• Most HMDs include integrated motion tracking to adjust the view based on the user's head movements.
 
 
 
• **Haptic Gloves:**
 
 
• Haptic gloves are designed to provide tactile feedback, simulating the sense of touch in VR environments.
 
• They allow users to interact with virtual objects in a more realistic and intuitive manner.
 
 
 
• **Limitations of Optical Mouse in VR:**
 
 
• An optical mouse is limited to surface-based 2D navigation and lacks 6 degrees of freedom (6DoF).
 
• It cannot provide immersive or precise interactions required in VR applications.
 
 
 
• **Importance of 6 Degrees of Freedom (6DoF):**
 
 
• 6DoF refers to the ability to track movements in three axes: forward/backward, up/down, left/right, along with pitch, yaw, and roll.
 
• Devices with 6DoF allow for a fully immersive experience, which is essential in VR environments.

questions.question:
What will the following PowerShell command in Windows OS do?

Command: Remove-Item C:\Logs -Recurse -Force

options.text: Delete only empty folders under C:\Logs
Move the C:\Logs folder to the Recycle Bin
Only delete files, leave folders intact
Delete all files and subfolders inside C:\Logs, including the folder itself

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Delete all files and subfolders inside C:\Logs, including the folder itself**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Remove-Item** cmdlet is used in PowerShell to delete files, folders, and other items.
 
• The **-Recurse** parameter ensures that the cmdlet deletes all items within a folder, including subfolders and their contents.
 
• The **-Force** parameter overrides restrictions, such as read-only attributes, allowing the deletion of protected files and folders.
 
• When executed, **Remove-Item C:\Logs -Recurse -Force** deletes the entire **C:\Logs** folder, including all files and subdirectories it contains.
 
• This command permanently deletes the folder and its contents, bypassing the Recycle Bin unless recovery software is used.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **PowerShell Command Syntax:**

 
 
• **Remove-Item**: Deletes specified items such as files, folders, and registry keys.
 
• **-Recurse**: Deletes items recursively, including all subfolders and their contents.
 
• **-Force**: Allows deletion of read-only, hidden, or system-protected items.
 
 
 
• **Precautions When Using Remove-Item:**
 
 
• Ensure you have backups of important data, as this command permanently deletes files.
 
• Review the path carefully to avoid unintentional deletions.
 
• Use the **-WhatIf** parameter to simulate the command and verify its actions before execution.
 
 
 
• **Alternative Commands for File Deletion:**
 
 
• **Del**: A simpler command for deleting files, but less versatile than **Remove-Item**.
 
• **rmdir**: Removes directories, but does not support advanced parameters like **-Recurse**.
 
 
 
• **Recovering Deleted Files:**
 
 
• Files deleted using **Remove-Item** with the **-Force** parameter are not sent to the Recycle Bin.
 
• Data recovery tools, such as Recuva or EaseUS Data Recovery, may be used to attempt recovery.

questions.question: Which of the following accurately explains why a touchscreen can be considered both an input and an output device?

options.text: It allows users to interact with visual data and sends touch signals to the computer.
It only displays images but responds to voice commands
It processes user data internally and sends it to memory
It stores programs and lets users write directly to memory.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It allows users to interact with visual data and sends touch signals to the computer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A touchscreen is a device that integrates both input and output functionalities in one interface.
 
• It displays visual data on the screen (output) and detects touch gestures/signals from users, such as taps or swipes (input).
 
• Touchscreens are commonly used in smartphones, tablets, ATMs, and other devices requiring direct user interaction.
 
• The ability to interpret touch and send signals to the computer makes it a key input device, while its display capability makes it an output device.
 
• Modern touchscreens often use capacitive or resistive technology to detect touch, enabling precise interaction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Capacitive Touchscreen Technology**

 
 
• Uses the electrical properties of the human body to detect touch.
 
• Highly responsive and supports multi-touch gestures like pinch-to-zoom.
 
• Commonly used in smartphones, tablets, and modern laptops.
 
 
 
• **Resistive Touchscreen Technology**
 
 
• Consists of two layers separated by a small gap; touch causes the layers to connect.
 
• Works with any object, including a stylus, unlike capacitive screens which require conductive touch.
 
• Frequently used in industrial and medical devices due to durability.
 
 
 
• **Input vs. Output Devices**
 
 
• Input devices allow users to send data to the computer (e.g., keyboard, mouse).
 
• Output devices display or present data from the computer (e.g., monitor, printer).
 
• Touchscreens combine both functionalities, making them unique hybrid devices.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Touchscreens**
 
 
• Widely used in consumer electronics, including smartphones, tablets, and smartwatches.
 
• Integrated into public systems such as kiosks, ATMs, and ticket machines.
 
• Enhanced usability in automotive dashboards and industrial machinery interfaces.

questions.question: Which type of memory is non-volatile and is used to store essential system instructions in a computer?

options.text: ROM
RAM
Registers
Cache Memory

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ROM**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **ROM (Read-Only Memory)** is a type of non-volatile memory used to store essential system instructions that remain intact even when the computer is powered off.
 
• It contains firmware, which is permanently written by the manufacturer and cannot be modified by the user under normal conditions.
 
• ROM is crucial for the booting process as it stores the **BIOS (Basic Input/Output System)** or UEFI firmware instructions.
 
• Unlike RAM, the data in ROM is persistent and not lost when the system is shut down, making it ideal for storing critical instructions.
 
• Examples of ROM include **EPROM (Erasable Programmable ROM)** and **EEPROM (Electrically Erasable Programmable ROM)**, which are more flexible variations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **RAM (Random Access Memory):**

 
 
• RAM is a volatile memory type used for temporary data storage while a program is running.
 
• It provides faster read and write speeds compared to ROM but loses all data when the computer is turned off.
 
 
 
• **Registers:**
 
 
• Registers are high-speed storage locations within the CPU used to store temporary data and instructions.
 
• They are much smaller in size but faster compared to both RAM and ROM.
 
 
 
• **Cache Memory:**
 
 
• Cache memory is a small-sized type of volatile memory located close to the CPU to store frequently accessed data and instructions.
 
• It significantly enhances the processing speed by reducing the time required to access data from the main memory.
 
 
 
• **Types of ROM:**
 
 
• **Masked ROM:** Pre-programmed at the time of manufacturing.
 
• **PROM:** Programmable Read-Only Memory that can be written once.
 
• **EPROM:** Can be erased using ultraviolet light and reprogrammed.
 
• **EEPROM:** Can be erased and reprogrammed electrically.

questions.question: Which of the following devices processes data in the computer system?

options.text: RAM
FDD
HDD
CPU

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**CPU**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Central Processing Unit (CPU) is often referred to as the **brain of the computer**, responsible for processing instructions and performing calculations.
 
• It executes programs by carrying out basic arithmetic, logic, control, and input/output (I/O) operations specified by the instructions.
 
• Modern CPUs consist of multiple cores, which enable **parallel processing** for enhanced performance.
 
• The CPU interacts with other components like RAM and storage devices to fetch, decode, and execute instructions efficiently.
 
• It operates using a clock speed measured in GHz, which determines how many instructions it can process per second.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **RAM (Random Access Memory):**

 
 
• RAM is a volatile memory used by the CPU to temporarily store data and instructions that are actively being used or processed.
 
• It enables faster access to data compared to storage devices like HDD or SSD.
 
• However, data in RAM is lost when the computer is powered off.
 
 
 
• **HDD (Hard Disk Drive):**
 
 
• An HDD is a non-volatile storage device used for storing large amounts of data permanently.
 
• It operates using magnetic storage and has slower read/write speeds compared to RAM.
 
• It is primarily used for storing the operating system, applications, and user data.
 
 
 
• **FDD (Floppy Disk Drive):**
 
 
• A floppy disk drive is an older storage device used to read and write data to floppy disks.
 
• It has largely been replaced by modern storage devices due to its limited capacity and slow speed.
 
 
 
• **CPU Components:**
 
 
• The CPU is composed of the Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU), which performs calculations and logical operations.
 
• The Control Unit (CU) directs operations by interpreting instructions and coordinating with other hardware components.
 
• Registers within the CPU temporarily store data and instructions for quick access.

questions.question: Which of the following statements DOES NOT describe the primary difference between SRAM and DRAM in terms of their internal architecture and performance characteristics?

options.text: DRAM is much faster because it has a simple design and doesn’t need refresh.
DRAM uses one transistor + one capacitor (1T1C) per cell (high density), while SRAM uses multiple transistors per bit (lower density).
SRAM is faster and more expensive → used for CPU caches; DRAM is slower and cheaper → used for main memory (RAM).
SRAM uses more transistors per bit, yielding faster access than DRAM.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1) “DRAM is much faster and doesn’t need to refresh.”**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Why Option 1 is invalid:** *DRAM* is **slower** than SRAM and it **does require periodic refresh** to retain data. The statement reverses both facts.
 
• **Actual DRAM cell:** Typically **1 transistor + 1 capacitor (1T1C)** per bit → *high density, low cost*, but needs refresh → *higher latency* than SRAM.
 
• **Actual SRAM cell:** Typically **multiple transistors (≈6T)** forming a bistable latch → *no refresh needed, faster access*, but *lower density and higher cost*.
 
• **Common usage:** *SRAM* → CPU **caches** (L1/L2/L3). *DRAM* → system **main memory** (DIMMs).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2 (Correct statement):** DRAM uses **1T1C** (compact, dense), while SRAM uses **multiple transistors** per bit (less dense).
 
• **Option 3 (Correct statement):** *SRAM* is faster and more expensive → used for **cache**; *DRAM* is slower and cheaper → used for **main memory**.
 
• **Option 4 (Correct statement):** SRAM’s multi-transistor latch enables **faster access** than DRAM’s capacitor-based cell.
 
• **Performance note:** Refresh operations and sense-amp charging in DRAM introduce extra delay; SRAM reads/writes directly from a stable latch.

__

• It helps in **streamlining navigation** during both the editing and presentation phases by dividing the slides into distinct sections.
 
• Sections allow users to **focus on specific parts** of the presentation without being overwhelmed by the entire slide deck.
 
• This feature is particularly useful when dealing with **complex or multi-topic presentations**, ensuring better structure and clarity.
 
• Users can **rename, collapse, or expand sections** for easier navigation, enhancing productivity in managing large presentations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Slide Organization in PowerPoint**

 
 
• PowerPoint includes features like 'Sections,' 'Slide Sorter View,' and 'Outline View' to help users manage and organize content efficiently.
 
• 'Slide Sorter View' provides a thumbnail view of all slides, enabling easier rearrangement.
 
• 'Outline View' focuses on text content, offering a structured view of the presentation.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of Using Sections**

• Improves workflow by allowing users to concentrate on specific sections.
 
• Reduces clutter and simplifies navigation in presentations with numerous slides.
 
 
 
• **Other Navigation Features in PowerPoint**
 
 
• Slide Master: Helps maintain consistent design across slides.
 
• Hyperlinks: Facilitates linking between slides or external resources.
 
• Slide Zoom: Enables focused navigation on specific slides during presentations.
 
 
 
• **PowerPoint for Large Presentations**
 
 
• For presentations with hundreds of slides, features like 'Sections' and 'Slide Sorter View' are essential for effective management.
 
• Grouping slides into sections ensures logical flow and improved audience engagement.

questions.question: Which of the following scenarios would most effectively necessitate the use of a three-dimensional reference within an MS Excel formula

options.text: Applying conditional formatting to a range of data based on values in another worksheet within the same workbook
Creating a chart that visualizes data points sourced from several different workbooks
Calculating the average sales figures across multiple non-contiguous worksheets for the same product category
Summing values from a specific cell across a sequence of identically structured worksheets representing monthly data for a year

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Summing values from a specific cell across a sequence of identically structured worksheets representing monthly data for a year**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A three-dimensional (3D) reference in MS Excel is used to reference the same cell or range of cells across multiple worksheets within the same workbook.
 
• It is particularly useful for performing calculations (e.g., summing, averaging) that involve data stored in the same cell position across identically structured worksheets.
 
• The correct scenario here—"Summing values from a specific cell across a sequence of identically structured worksheets representing monthly data for a year"—requires referencing the same cell (e.g., B2) across worksheets such as "Jan," "Feb," "Mar," etc.
 
• An example of a 3D reference formula for summing cell B2 across worksheets "Jan" to "Dec" would be: =SUM(Jan:Dec!B2).
 
• This method simplifies complex calculations and avoids manually navigating to each worksheet, making it efficient for managing large datasets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **3D Reference in MS Excel**

 
 
• A 3D reference allows users to refer to the same range or cell across multiple worksheets.
 
• It is denoted by the syntax: Sheet1:SheetN!CellReference.
 
• Common functions used with 3D references include SUM, AVERAGE, COUNT, MAX, and MIN.
 
 
 
• **Conditional Formatting vs. 3D References**
 
 
• Conditional formatting applies visual formatting rules to data within a single worksheet or across specific ranges, but it does not use 3D references.
 
• 3D references are designed for computations rather than formatting tasks.
 
 
 
• **Identically Structured Worksheets**
 
 
• These are worksheets that share the same layout, such as having the same rows, columns, and headings.
 
• Identical structure is a prerequisite for effectively using 3D references.
 
 
 
• **Advantages of 3D References**
 
 
• Enables efficient data analysis across multiple worksheets.
 
• Reduces redundancy by avoiding repetitive formulas for each worksheet.
 
• Improves consistency and minimizes human error in calculations.
 
 
 
• **Limitations of 3D References**
 
 
• 3D references cannot be used in array formulas or with certain Excel features like Data Tables.
 
• Deleting or rearranging worksheets within the referenced range may lead to formula errors.

questions.question: In Windows 11 OS, which of the following is NOT allowed in a file or folder name?

options.text: Hyphens (-)
Underscores (_)
Symbols like asterisk (*) or question mark (?)
Letters and numbers

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3,"

__Key Points__

__
 
• Windows operating systems, including Windows 11, prohibit the use of certain special characters in file and folder names.
 
• Characters such as **asterisks (*), question marks (?), colons (:), slashes (/ \), angle brackets (), pipes (|), quotation marks ("")**, and others are reserved for system use and cannot be included in file or folder names.
 
• These restrictions are implemented to avoid conflicts with the file system and ensure proper functioning of the operating system.
 
• Hyphens (-), underscores (_), letters, and numbers are allowed in file and folder names, as they do not interfere with system processes.
 
• Attempting to use restricted characters will result in an error message from Windows, preventing the creation or renaming of the file or folder.

**Additional Information__**

 
• **File System in Windows:**

 
 
• Windows primarily uses the NTFS (New Technology File System), which governs how data is stored and retrieved on a disk.
 
• NTFS supports features like file permissions, encryption, and large file sizes.
 
• It enforces character restrictions to maintain system integrity and compatibility.
 
 
 
• **Reserved Characters:**
 
 
• Characters like **asterisks (*)** and **question marks (?)** are used as wildcards in search and command-line operations.
 
• Other reserved characters include **angle brackets ()** for redirection and **pipes (|)** for command chaining.
 
 
 
• **File Naming Best Practices:**
 
 
• Use descriptive names to make files easier to identify.
 
• Avoid excessively long file names, as some applications may face issues handling them.
 
• Stick to alphanumeric characters, underscores (_), and hyphens (-) for compatibility across different systems.
 
 
 
• **System Reserved Names:**
 
 
• Windows prohibits file and folder names like **CON, PRN, AUX, NUL**, and others, as they are reserved for system devices.
 
• These restrictions apply regardless of file extension.
